queries.title: Claude Agent SDK (Rust): SDK-hosted in-process MCP servers (tool + createSdkMcpServer)
queries.body:
Add the Rust equivalent of the TS SDK's `tool()` + `createSdkMcpServer()` to `crates/claude_agent_sdk`: custom tools defined in Rust that run inside the host process.

- `SdkMcpServer` builder (name, version, `.tool(name, description, input_schema, async handler)`), `ToolResult` with text, image and `is_error` content.
- `QueryOptions::sdk_mcp_server` registers it in `initialize.sdkMcpServers` (plus `sdkMcpServerConfigs`, optional `sdkMcpServerManifests`).
- Route `mcp_message` control requests to it and answer per JSON-RPC (initialize, tools/list, tools/call, ping, notifications).
- `mcp__<server>__<tool>` names for `allowed_tools`.
- Unit tests, fake-CLI tests, a live smoke example, PARITY.md and README.

Needed by the briefed agent in #11211.

queries.title: Coder: watch the whole issue → PR run in the terminal (decision steps + briefed Claude subagent)
queries.body:
Build a one-off run that takes an issue number and plays the whole issue → PR flow inside the standard Coder terminal, as a test run.

**Decision steps (#11210):** each stage shows as a new, distinct decision card:
- the file-finding stages;
- each classifier or model call: question, options, probabilities, the chosen answer, which door answered, latency and cost;
- the resulting ranked file list and the briefing.

**The briefed Claude subagent (#11211, on crates/claude_agent_sdk):** its work shows with Coder's usual tool-call rendering (Read, Edit, Grep, Run checks, diffs), live.

**The end:** a summary card with time, tokens, $, files missed versus the briefing, whether checks passed, and the diff. In test mode it goes no further than a local branch or diff; opening a PR is an explicit opt-in.

**Done when** one command (e.g. `coder issue-run N`) on a closed or open issue shows the whole flow in the terminal, and a recorded run plus a screenshot are in docs.

queries.title: Training corpus from the file-finder bench: train, calibration and locked splits (roadmap N8)
queries.body:
Turn the #11210 bench data (closed issues with `(#N)` fix commits, the finder's candidates and the changed-file labels) into a decision-training corpus in the `tenancy::training` format.

- **Splits:** train / calibration / locked, split by time (no fix may sit in an earlier split than an older fix), with the newest fixes held out.
- **Labels:** each row records its evidence class. Labels come from outcomes; Jev answers are kept only as a teacher field.

**Done when:** the corpus builds reproducibly from git with one command, and its manifest and digests are committed (the data itself stays out of git). See docs/audits/2026-10-10-training-system-audit/roadmap.md.

queries.title: Calibrate Clef-Flash's file-relevance probabilities (roadmap X1)
queries.body:
Clef-Flash ranks files well but its probabilities run low (F1 0.44 at 0.5, from the batch-prompt bench).

- Measure its raw F1 and ECE on the N8 corpus's development split.
- Fit a per-question temperature or Platt map on the calibration split.
- Ship the map as a versioned file the Clef path applies.

**Done when:** ECE drops and F1 at 0.5 improves on the locked split, with the numbers in docs/inference/clef-native.md. Depends on the N8 corpus issue.

queries.title: Train a head-only file-relevance ranker on the finder's candidates (roadmap X2a)
queries.body:
Train a small learned interface on top of the frozen deterministic finder (Tassadar W3 design law: frozen exact core, learned interface).

- **Inputs:** the finder's deterministic features plus Clef's cached final hidden rows.
- **Where:** psionic-train, CPU or the 4080; serve exports hidden rows to a file, with no train→serve crate dependency.

**Done when:** it is compared with today's numpy ranker on the bench and on the newer-fix set (currently 0.85 at 400). It ships only if it wins there by at least 2 standard errors without worse calibration. Depends on the N8 corpus and calibration issues.

queries.title: Capture verify-replayed outcomes from issue-run and A/B runs as labelled traces (roadmap X11)
queries.body:
Every `coder issue-run` and #11211 A/B run becomes a training trace, but only after an independent replay.

- **Replay:** re-run verify at the same commit on another machine or a clean worktree and compare digests.
- **Labels from the actual diff:** files changed, files opened late, checks result and acceptance. Never from the agent's own summary.
- **Each trace records:** its evidence class and a replay receipt.
- **Feeds:** filefind feedback and the N8 corpus.

**Done when:** at least 20 replayed traces are admitted and one is visibly rejected for a digest mismatch in a test.

queries.title: Chat worker: Gemini on Vertex AI as the first door, Vertex embeddings
queries.body:
OpenRouter is at -$2.52 and the Vercel AI Gateway answers 402, so production chat on oa-coder-worker-1 is degraded (embeddings failing every 45 s, Gemini only through OpenRouter). Put Gemini on Vertex AI (project openagentsgemini, prepaid Google credit) first for chat generation and embeddings, keep OpenRouter and Vercel as fallbacks, and deploy.

Code: e70c410dda.

queries.title: Google first: every model and embedding call on our keys goes to Vertex AI first
queries.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-10: use the prepaid Google credit (GCP openagentsgemini) first for every model and embedding call on our keys; OpenRouter (out of credit) and the Vercel AI Gateway (402) become fallbacks.

Scope:
- docs/inference/providers.md: every call site, first door, fallbacks; BYOK and user-machine rows marked.
- Vertex embeddings first for the file finder (scripts/filefind) and other house-key embedding paths, with index model matching.
- Coder default paths on our key: Gemini on Vertex first via coder::generate::vertex_door_from_env / Door::behind.

Not in scope here: the inference gateway router, chat_vision, coder-new web_search (other owners), BYOK paths.

queries.title: Google first: web chat vision and coder-new web_search on Gemini/Vertex, current providers as fallbacks
queries.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-10: use Google (prepaid GCP credit, project openagentsgemini) first, other providers as fallbacks (OpenRouter is negative, Vercel AI Gateway returns 402).

1. Web chat vision door (crates/openagents-web/src/chat_vision.rs): images and PDFs go to gemini-3.8-flash on Vertex AI first (inlineData parts via the inference crate's Vertex adapter body), then the gateway Open Responses door, then the hosted chat words-only.
2. coder-new web_search (crates/coder-new/src/web_tools.rs): Gemini with Google Search grounding on Vertex first (answer + groundingChunks sources), then Exa, then OpenRouter; the failover reason is kept in the result.

Production: the openagents.com web container (Cloud Run service coder) gets the Vertex service-account key secret, deployed via scripts/deploy/web.sh.

queries.title: Inference gateway: Gemini on Vertex AI first on every class it can serve
queries.body:
Owner direction (2026-10-10): use Google first everywhere; we hold about $30,000 of prepaid Google credit on `openagentsgemini`, while OpenRouter is at -$2.52 and the Vercel AI Gateway answers 402.

Scope: the inference gateway (`crates/inference` router, `crates/gateway`).

- Gemini on Vertex AI first in every class it can serve: `classify` (Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite), `fast` and `chat` (Gemini 3.8 Flash), `long`; so `openagents/auto` too. Other upstreams stay behind it in their earlier order.
- `google/gemini-3.8-flash` by model id (the Environments setup agent) already ranks Vertex first by the prepaid-credit rule; verify.
- Deploy the new gateway image to staging (`openagents-web-1-staging`) and production (`coder`), verify a real request answers from upstream `vertex`, record rollback.
- `code` and `reason` keep the Pro door first: Vertex has no Gemini Pro id in the adapter (`gemini-3.8-pro` is 404 on Vertex).

queries.title: Cloud environments hand Mac-only steps to a linked Mac (Xcode, iOS builds, TestFlight, macOS checks)
queries.body:
Development is moving onto our production environment (docs/cloud/dogfood-dev-on-prod.md). Some steps can only run on macOS: Xcode and iOS builds, TestFlight upload (`scripts/release/asc.py`, `tf.sh`), macOS UI tests, and desktop app captures.

**Goal:** a cloud environment, or an agent in one, can send those steps to a Mac that is linked to the account, and get the results back without anyone touching the Mac.

**Build on what exists:**
- the Coder link and computer ops (NIP-HOST, #11171/#11185 screenshot and files);
- the own-runs channel from #11080, where the computer pulls work and streams progress;
- deploy approvals (#11170).

**Needs:**
- The Mac advertises its capabilities (macOS, Xcode version, signing identities available, simulators).
- The environment sends a typed job: build, test, upload or capture, with a repo ref.
- The Mac pulls the job, checks out that ref in its own worktree, runs it, and streams logs.
- Artifacts come back to the environment: .ipa/.app, test results, screenshots.
- Signing and App Store keys never leave the Mac.
- Store uploads and anything else outward-facing need the owner's approval.

**Done when:** an agent in a cloud environment runs the iOS release gate UI tests and a TestFlight upload on the linked Mac, end to end, with the logs and the result visible on web and phone.

queries.title: Coder host image bake fails since 2026-10-07: 100 GB builder disk too small for the warm target
queries.body:
The daily `oa-coder-host-image-daily` bake has failed four days running (2026-10-07..10). The newest image is `oa-coder-host-20261006`.

The 2026-10-10 log ends at the `microcoder` warm build:

```
openagents lease: builds are refused below the free-space floor plus the builds' disk budgets: 7.7 GB free, and a build needs 20 GB, where the floor is 10 GB.
OA_CODER_HOST_BAKE_FAILED line=81 status=1
```

The workspace's warm target no longer fits the 100 GB builder disk (`scripts/cloud/build-coder-host-image.sh`, `DISK_GB` default 100).

Fix: bake on a 200 GB disk, and give pool hosts (`crates/coder-cloud/src/pool.rs` `DISK_GB`) 300 GB so a host built from a 200 GB image still has room for a second slot. Part of moving OpenAgents development onto our own environments (docs/cloud/dogfood-dev-on-prod.md). This issue is the end-to-end proof: done by an agent on a cloud environment, no MacBook.

queries.title: Decisions with no Jev dependency: our /v1/systemone farms NIP-DEC jobs to connected Pylons (Clef), Vertex Gemini as fallback
queries.body:
Owner, 2026-10-10: every decision (router, judges, file relevance, Verse questions) must go through our own API, which farms the jobs out to connected Pylons over Nostr. No dependency on the Jev API.

**What exists:**
- NIP-DEC decision jobs (kinds 25910/26910/27010; `crates/nostr` decision; the gateway's `decision-worker`, `decision_offer.rs`);
- NIP-PYLON beacons and receipts;
- Clef on Psionic `/v1/systemone` (M1 CPU, M2 CUDA, #11194/#11195);
- the jev client's door chain (`crates/jev/src/doors.rs`).

**Build:**
1. **Dispatch.** The gateway's `POST /v1/systemone` becomes the one decision entry point. It picks a connected Pylon whose NIP-PYLON beacon advertises a decision service (a Clef model and its identity) with free slots. It sends a NIP-DEC request, waits for the result with a deadline, and checks the answer's shape and model identity. Then it fails over to the next Pylon.
2. **Pylon side.** A Pylon running Psionic's Clef server answers NIP-DEC jobs and advertises them in its beacon. This is free work only for now; payments are not V1 and Bitcoin-only later. #11191 and #11192 are folded in.
3. **Fallback chain.** Connected Pylons (Clef) first; then our own hosted Clef (CoderOS 4080 / a Cloud GPU); then Vertex Gemini answering the same typed question with structured output. Jev is optional and last, off by default.
4. **Clients switch.** Every caller of the jev crate or TypeSafe goes to our endpoint, with no hard-coded TypeSafe URL in the default path: the coder router and judges, coder-new, coder-delegate, the Verse, filefind, issue-run, the A/B harness and ext-eval.
5. **Evidence.** Each answer records which Pylon or door answered, the model identity, latency and agreement samples. A shadow share is sent to a second door so quality is visible.

**Done when:** production chat routing and Coder's judges run with the Jev key removed from their environment, answered by a connected Pylon (CoderOS-4080 as the first one), with failover proven by stopping that Pylon.

queries.title: Web Environments: push to the repository with the owner's GitHub connection
queries.body:
Gap 10 of docs/cloud/dogfood-dev-on-prod.md. Environment setup machines and Claude Code runs get no GitHub credential today (docs/deployment/agent-work.md: public repositories only), so a run on openagents.com cannot push its change or open a pull request.

Do: hand each run a short-lived, repository-scoped token from the signed-in person's GitHub connection (never a server-wide token), so a Claude Code run in an environment can push a branch, open a PR and, with approval, land on main. Private repositories follow.

Acceptance: from openagents.com, a Claude Code run in an OpenAgentsInc/openagents environment pushes a branch and opens a PR; the token is never stored in the image or printed.

queries.title: Integrator on a cloud environment: one landing queue, idle stop
queries.body:
Gaps 12 and 15 of docs/cloud/dogfood-dev-on-prod.md. On the Mac one integrator agent builds, tests and lands agents' work one at a time. The issue flow's --land main lands each issue on its own with rebase and checks, but nothing holds one queue across hosts, and the big environment (oa-dev-env-1, c3-standard-22, 300 GB) has no idle stop.

Do: run the integrator on the environment with a single landing queue (agents push branches; the integrator rebases, builds with sccache, tests, pushes main, closes, moves the board), and stop the VM after N idle minutes the way pool hosts delete themselves.

Acceptance: three agents' branches land in order from the environment with no Mac; the VM stops itself when idle.

queries.title: Fleet rows for cloud environment runs: watch them from web and phone
queries.body:
Gap 13 of docs/cloud/dogfood-dev-on-prod.md. Runs on a GCE environment or pool host show only in issue comments, runs.jsonl on the orchestrating computer and the serial console. They should show in the web agent fleet (#11164) and on the phone as AgentRow rows (crates/agent-fleet), with stop and message.

Acceptance: an issue run started on oa-dev-env-1 appears in the web fleet list and the phone, live, and can be stopped from either.

queries.title: Runner: verify/finish never report success without a passing run; cache bound to full candidate content (audit A01, A02 — P0)
queries.body:
**RUN-01:** a nonzero exit, a spawn error, a timeout, invalid output, a missing target, or zero required tests must never become `pass`. `finish` must not trust a cached verdict.

**RUN-02:** reuse of a verification result must be keyed on the complete candidate. That means staged, unstaged, untracked and removed content, the test scope, and the checker identity. Never on filenames alone.

Fix both in `crates/briefed-agent` (verify, tools), with a test for each failure state. This is P0: the success signal can't be trusted for acceptance or learning until it lands.

Source: the self-improving codebases audit, `docs/audits/2026-10-10-self-improving-codebases-audit` (README, 02/03/06, action register in 09-roadmap-and-acceptance.md).

queries.title: issue-run: own worktree per run, no PR or success on failed final checks, full attempt and unknown-cost inventory (audit A03, A06, A09)
queries.body:
- **RUN-03:** a failed required check or an agent error cannot lead to delivery or PR creation. Optional checks are reported separately.
- **RUN-06:** every `coder issue-run` gets its own scratch worktree. Starting a run never deletes another run's active or uncaptured work.
- **PRODUCT-03/04 (A09):** failed setups, retries and cancellations survive export, and missing usage or cost stays *unknown*, never 0. That applies to the trace capture too (`scripts/bench/traces`).

Owner: `crates/coder-new` (issue_run) plus the trace capture.

Source: the self-improving codebases audit, `docs/audits/2026-10-10-self-improving-codebases-audit` (README, 02/03/06, action register in 09-roadmap-and-acceptance.md).

queries.title: Learning integrity: gated ranker activation, one partition map across feeds, replayed-only labels (audit A12, A13, A15)
queries.body:
- **LEARN-01:** `retrain.sh` writes a candidate model. It never overwrites the shipped one. Overlapping train/eval sets are refused. The old model stays active until a protected comparison passes and the new one is explicitly promoted.
- **LEARN-02:** replayed traces take their partition from the #11215 corpus map (issue groups). The 41 admitted traces must not move calibration or development groups into training.
- **LEARN-04:** raw run feedback may help exploration but is labelled an observation. Only replayed, partition-eligible outcomes count as learning labels or affect the shipped retrieval.

Owners: `scripts/filefind`, `scripts/bench/traces`, the #11215 corpus.

Source: the self-improving codebases audit, `docs/audits/2026-10-10-self-improving-codebases-audit` (README, 02/03/06, action register in 09-roadmap-and-acceptance.md).

queries.title: Data boundary: teacher content removed on corpus deletion; finder caches and feedback namespaced per repository and workspace (audit A22, A23)
queries.body:
- **DATA-03:** deleting a corpus item removes its state, question, label *and* teacher content. Linked exports, caches and checkpoints are handled explicitly (`tenancy::training`).
- **DATA-04:** filefind caches and feedback are keyed by a stable repository identity (remote URL plus root commit) and workspace. Two repos with the same basename or the same issue numbers never share state.

Required before S5 (second repository) and any customer learning.

Source: the self-improving codebases audit, `docs/audits/2026-10-10-self-improving-codebases-audit` (README, 02/03/06, action register in 09-roadmap-and-acceptance.md).

queries.title: Claude plan usage from Claude Code itself: rate_limit_event and get_usage, shown in Coder, desktop, web and Cloud jobs
queries.body:
Plan: [`docs/byok/claude-plan.md`](https://github.com/OpenAgentsInc/openagents/blob/main/docs/byok/claude-plan.md), item "Plan usage you can see".

Claude Pro and Max have a five-hour window, a weekly window, and (Max) a separate weekly Fable cap. Claude Code itself reports where a plan stands, through Anthropic's own binary, without anyone reading the login:

- every `claude -p --output-format stream-json` run and every `claude_agent_sdk` session emits `rate_limit_event` (`status`, `rateLimitType`, `utilization`, `resetsAt`, `overageStatus`, `overageResetsAt`), already typed as `SdkRateLimitInfo` in `crates/claude_agent_sdk/src/protocol/messages.rs` and partly read by `crates/microcoder-loop/src/claude.rs`;
- the SDK's `Query::get_usage` (the structured `/usage` payload) answers on demand.

Today the only full reading is the owner-host usage probe (`crates/coder/src/task/usage.rs`), which reads the Claude OAuth token from the keychain and calls `api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage`. It is opt-in and owner-only (INVARIANTS row on usage probes) and must not become the path for anyone else.

**Do**
1. Record the latest `rate_limit_event` from every Claude Code run (local Coder, Cloud `claude_print`, briefed agent, Studio seats) into the usage book (`usage.json`) as typed windows, with the login fingerprint rule unchanged. Ask `get_usage` once at session start where an SDK session exists.
2. Make that the default reading. The keychain probe stays an owner-host opt-in fallback.
3. Show it: Coder's status line ("Claude plan: 5h 62% · week 31% · resets 14:20"), the desktop engine row, the web Workbench / environment status (`coder_engine_status::Status` gains closed-enum window kind + percent + reset, still no strings), and the Cloud job card.
4. A warning (`allowed_warning`) shows as a quiet note, not a stop.

**Acceptance**
- [ ] Fixture streams with each `rateLimitType` produce the right typed reading (test).
- [ ] No code path added here reads a credential file or keychain item (test asserts the Cloud and SDK paths never open `.credentials.json`).
- [ ] Status line and web Workbench show the windows from a fixture run.

queries.title: Pick Claude Code, then connect: inline Sign in to Claude in web, desktop and mobile, plus clear local not-found / not-signed-in cards
queries.body:
Plan: [`docs/byok/claude-plan.md`](https://github.com/OpenAgentsInc/openagents/blob/main/docs/byok/claude-plan.md), item "Connect a Claude plan".

Amp's flow (https://ampcode.com/news/use-your-claude-plan): pick Mode > Claude Code when starting a thread; if no Claude plan is linked, it asks right there. We want the same moment, done our way: the sign-in always completes in Anthropic's own flow inside the unmodified `claude` binary on the person's computer or their own environment.

Today: Settings → Claude saves a key or `setup-token` value (`crates/openagents-web/src/settings.rs`, `cloud/byo.rs`); the Workbench has "Sign in to Claude" for Cloud computers (BYO-01, #11008); "Claude Code in REPO" runs (#11162) need a key saved in Settings first, and a run without one is a dead end.

**Do**
1. Web new chat, desktop, and mobile: choosing Claude Code (or "Claude Code in REPO") with nothing signed in shows one inline card: **Sign in to Claude** (opens the environment's terminal running `claude`, Anthropic's browser flow, code pasted back there) and **Use a key instead** (links to Settings → Claude). After sign-in the queued message runs with no retyping.
2. The login made inside an environment persists only in that person's own checkpoint (rule 4 of `docs/cloud/claude-code-byo.md`), so it is once per environment.
3. Local Coder on the person's own computer: clear cards for "Claude Code not found" (look in `$PATH`, `~/.local/bin`, `~/bin`; give the one-line install `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash`), "Not signed in" (run `claude`, then `/login`), and "Can't run as root", each with **Retry**.

**Acceptance**
- [ ] Picking Claude Code with no sign-in shows the card, never an error after send (test on web).
- [ ] After sign-in in a fixture environment, the held message runs (test with the fixture `claude`).
- [ ] Each local failure card has the exact command and a working Retry.

queries.title: Settings, Claude: sign in inside the environment first, subscription-token custody limited to an allowlist until Anthropic approves, Max/Team API-credits path
queries.body:
Plan: [`docs/byok/claude-plan.md`](https://github.com/OpenAgentsInc/openagents/blob/main/docs/byok/claude-plan.md), item "The terms question".

Anthropic's help center now says plainly that the Agent SDK, `claude -p`, and third-party apps can use a Claude plan's limits (https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15036540-use-the-claude-agent-sdk-with-your-claude-plan). Its Claude Code legal page still says developers may not offer Claude.ai login in their own apps, route requests through plan credentials on their users' behalf, or collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens; sign-in must complete through Anthropic's own flow (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance). The Agent SDK overview says "Unless previously approved". So signing in to the unmodified binary inside the person's own computer or environment is the sanctioned path; our server keeping a `claude setup-token` value (#11204) is not covered without Anthropic's written approval.

**Do**
1. Settings → Claude puts **Sign in inside your environment** first and explains it; the API key and cloud-credential options stay as they are.
2. The subscription-token option is shown and accepted only for accounts on an allowlist (default: the owner's account), behind a server flag, until the owner records Anthropic's approval. Existing saved tokens for other accounts keep working until removed, with a notice to switch to in-environment sign-in. Update `docs/cloud/claude-code-byo.md` rule 2 and the matching `INVARIANTS.md` row in the same change.
3. Copy for Max and Team: those plans include monthly API credits ($100 Max 5x, $200 Max 20x, pooled per seat on Team, capped at $500) claimable into a Claude Console organization (https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17154008-monthly-api-credits-for-max-and-team-plans). A key from that organization is an ordinary API key: it runs tasks in parallel and bills those credits, not the plan.

**Acceptance**
- [ ] A non-allowlisted account cannot see or save a subscription token (test); an allowlisted one can.
- [ ] The gateway still refuses subscription tokens (`inference_byok::admit_key`, unchanged).
- [ ] Policy doc and INVARIANTS updated in the same commit.

queries.title: When a Claude plan runs out: offer continue on your own key or with OpenAgents (Vertex Gemini), never Claude billed to us
queries.body:
Plan: [`docs/byok/claude-plan.md`](https://github.com/OpenAgentsInc/openagents/blob/main/docs/byok/claude-plan.md), item "When the plan runs out".

Today a Cloud Claude Code task that hits the plan limit pauses until the reset Claude Code reported and resumes on its own (BYO-03, `coder_cloud::claude_task`); the local chat does the same (#11179). Local Coder's provider order already falls back Codex → Claude → our Vertex cloud worker (`microcoder_loop::capacity::Provider::Vertex`).

**Do**: when a Claude plan pauses, the pause card offers choices instead of only waiting:
1. **Keep waiting** (default; resumes at the reset).
2. **Continue on your key**: if the person saved an Anthropic API key or their own Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry credential, the same Claude Code session continues on it (Claude Code's own `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX` path for their Vertex).
3. **Continue with OpenAgents**: hand the rest of the task to Coder's own agent on our Vertex Gemini door (Google first), billed as our normal usage.

Never: continue a customer's Claude Code session on Claude models billed to our account (Anthropic's terms forbid paying for or intermediating a user's Claude Code usage), and never buy Anthropic "extra usage" for them.

**Acceptance**
- [ ] A fixture limit offers exactly the choices the person's saved credentials allow (test).
- [ ] Choice 2 never sends a subscription token; choice 3 never starts `claude`.

queries.title: Local Coder: one automated run at a time on a Claude plan login by default, person-set limit, interactive chats never queued
queries.body:
Plan: [`docs/byok/claude-plan.md`](https://github.com/OpenAgentsInc/openagents/blob/main/docs/byok/claude-plan.md), item "One task at a time on a plan".

Cloud already admits one automated Claude turn at a time on a plan login or subscription token (`coder_cloud::claude::admit_turns`, rule 7). Local Coder does not: background agents and auto-started tasks can each start `claude` on the same plan login at once. Anthropic's limits "assume ordinary, individual usage of Claude Code and the Agent SDK".

**Do**
1. Local auto-started and background runs on a Claude plan login use one plan slot by default; more queue, with "waiting for your Claude plan" on their card. The person can raise the number in Settings (their own limit), and an API key login is never limited.
2. Interactive chats the person types into are never queued.
3. A `rate_limit_event` with `allowed_warning` makes the queue hold new automated starts until the window reports under the warning.

**Acceptance**
- [ ] Two background starts on a plan login run one after the other by default (test); with an API key they run together.
- [ ] The person's setting changes the number and is never overridden.

queries.title: Connections: third-party data and tools (Google Drive first) in projects, web chat, Coder and the apps
queries.body:
Owner request, 2026-10-10: connect third-party software (Google Drive, accounting, bank, …) to our UI. Example: the `finances` project pulls in data from Google Drive.

**Decision:** build it natively in Rust, with no third-party runtime dependency. Harvest the design from UsefulSoftwareCo/executor (MIT; reference clone at `projects/repos/executor`, see its vision.md):
- **Integration:** produced from a spec (OpenAPI / GraphQL / Google Discovery / MCP).
- **Connection:** a named credential per account (`work`, `personal`).
- **SecretRef:** the agent never sees the secret; a provider resolves it at call time.
- **Scope:** account / workspace / project.
- **Per-tool policy:** allow / require-approval / block, with defaults from the HTTP method (reads allowed, writes need approval).
- **Address:** `<integration>.<scope>.<connection>.<tool>`, with tools searchable by intent.

**V1 slice (Google first):**
1. **Settings → Connections:** connect Google (OAuth, `drive.readonly` + `spreadsheets.readonly`, incremental consent) using our existing Google sign-in, from a Google Cloud OAuth client in `openagentsgemini`. Tokens are sealed per account like the other BYO credentials.
2. **Project sources:** a project can attach Drive folders or files as sources (e.g. `finances` → a Drive folder).
3. **Tools,** available in web chat, Coder (`coder-new` tool registry) and `/mcp`: `drive.search`, `drive.read` (Docs as text, Sheets as CSV, PDFs as text), `drive.list_folder`. Read-only, so allowed by default.
4. **In chat:** "summarize my spending this month" in the finances project reads the attached Sheets and answers, citing the files used, Google-first (Vertex).

**Next:** generic OpenAPI-spec integrations, per-tool policy UI, and accounting/bank connectors (e.g. QuickBooks/Xero, Plaid or bank CSV import), with writes always behind approval.

**Done when:** in the finances project on production, the owner connects Google, attaches a Drive folder, and asks a question that is answered from those files.

queries.title: Support the Personal Agent Protocol (Poppy, personalagentprotocol.org): our agents as clients, openagents.com as a Company
queries.body:
Low priority; not V1. The [Personal Agent Protocol](https://personalagentprotocol.org/) ("Poppy", Apache 2.0, draft 0.1, [spec](https://personalagentprotocol.org/docs/spec)) lets personal agents discover companies, sign the user in, and act through the company's APIs, MCP servers, website or company agent. Access is graduated: blocked / search / view / act with approval / full.

**What the spec defines:**
- **Discovery:** `/.well-known/poppy.json` with `protocol_version`, `organization`, `auth` (issuer; direct/device/mediated sign-in and scopes `poppy:read`/`poppy:write`), `agent.protocols[]` (a conversation endpoint), `apis[]` (`openapi` or `mcp`), `web.browser_session_endpoint` and `extensions`. It must agree with RFC 8414 metadata (`issuer` match, `poppy_domains`).
- **Agent identity:** `client_id` is an HTTPS URL to client metadata, with `jwks_uri` and `private_key_jwt`.
- **Sessions:** a jwt-bearer grant whose `sub` is an opaque, non-PII per-company user id. The response is `access_token` / `session_id` / `signed_in`. **DPoP** is required everywhere except MCP, which takes a Bearer token with `resource`.
- **Sign-in:** direct (authorization code + PKCE with an `iss` check), device (RFC 8628), or mediated (credentials posted only to the company endpoint; secrets never logged or shown to the model). The Account Token is a refresh token kept out of model context. Sign-out revokes it (RFC 7009).
- **Web binding:** a `poppy-browser+jwt` assertion, sent as a form POST, sets the session cookie.
- **Conversations:** `POST {endpoint}`, `/{id}/messages`, `/{id}/events` (cursor, SSE), `/handoff` and `/close`. Messages carry `sender` (agent/human, with `human` used only for the user's own words), `text`, `data` and `context`; status is working/idle/queued/closed; Direct Conversations hand the user to a person.

**Where it fits us:**
1. **Client side (main value).** Coder, web chat and agents act for the user at Poppy companies:
   - **Discover:** fetch and check `poppy.json`.
   - **Identity:** an OpenAgents client metadata document, with keys held server-side, never in model context.
   - **Sign-in and tools:** sign in through our approval UI (#11170-style). OpenAPI and MCP APIs become tools in the Connections catalog (#11238).
   - **Scopes:** reads are allowed; writes need approval.
   - **Messaging the company agent:** typed messages, rendered as cards.
   - **Credentials:** account tokens are sealed like the other BYO credentials.
2. **Company side.** openagents.com publishes `poppy.json` pointing at our existing OAuth server (#11084), `/mcp` and the OpenAPI document (#11157), so other people's personal agents can use OpenAgents. This needs DPoP and the jwt-bearer session grant on our token endpoint, and a reserved-scope mapping onto our key scopes (#11160).
3. **Reuse.** We already have RFC 8414/9728 metadata, PKCE, a device flow (`coder login`) and an MCP resource server. The gaps are DPoP, `private_key_jwt` client auth, the session grant and the conversation endpoint.

**Done when:**
- Coder can complete one task at a reference Poppy company (or our own test company) end to end, with sign-in and approvals.
- openagents.com's `poppy.json` passes an independent client's discovery and session flow.

The spec is draft 0.1 and may change incompatibly, so track it before building.

queries.title: Sensitive data vault: sealed (Tier B) financial data with a user share, Only-me opt-in, honest Tier C
queries.body:
Owner request, 2026-10-10: store people's sensitive data (first: uploaded financial statements and Google Drive finance files) so it can't be stolen or seen, ideally by anyone, including us.

**Spec:** `docs/security/sensitive-data-vault.md`. **Wire format:** draft `nips/openagents/NIP-VAULT.md`. **Attested workloads and the public release log:** draft `nips/openagents/NIP-ATT.md`.

**Decision (recommended in the spec):**
- Ship **Tier B** first for financial data. Files are encrypted on the person's device. Each file's key is wrapped with HPKE mode_psk to a per-person system key, and that system key's private half is released by Cloud KMS only to an attested vault image (Intel TDX, Confidential Space, `STABLE`, admitted digest). The person's client must supply its share on every request. No human, the owner included, holds a decrypt grant.
- **Tier A "Only me"** is an opt-in.
- Ordinary chats stay **Tier C**, honestly labelled ("Our team can read them") and KMS-logged.

**Milestones and gates (each gate passes on the deployed build):**
- [ ] **V0, honest Tier C.** CMEK and a KMS envelope for new attachments; KMS Data Access logs; vault data excluded from training.
  - Gate: a restore with the key disabled fails. Training refuses vault provenance.
- [ ] **V1, client core.** `oa-vault` crate (Rust + WASM): VMK, slots (passkey PRF, device, Nostr, recovery code), chunked AES-GCM, wraps, NIP-VAULT vectors.
  - Gate: vectors pass. A server-blindness canary scan finds nothing.
- [ ] **V2, sealed key release.** `openagents-vault` GCP project, HSM key ring, attested workload identity pool (TDX + `STABLE` + digest), deny policies, public Admin Activity export, vault workload on `c3-standard` TDX.
  - Gate: **owner-role principal gets `PERMISSION_DENIED` on Decrypt**. Debug image and non-admitted digest refused. Policy drift shows in the public log within 10 minutes.
- [ ] **V3, release log.** NIP-ATT `3202`/`30202`, Rekor, reproducible build with two matching builders, 7-day notice, opt-in per-person approval.
  - Gate: the client refuses an unadmitted, early or unapproved digest.
- [ ] **V4, product.** Finances project vault, sealed attachments, Fast route on Vertex (cache off), leases with Active access and Stop, export, crypto-shredding (24 h destroy window).
  - Gate: an expired lease is refused. After the destroy window, restored soft-deleted objects do not decrypt.
- [ ] **V5, Private route** via the private-inference issue (TDX + H100 Confidential Space).
- [ ] **V6, Tier A "Only me"** in the apps, plus Coder unlock and plaintext cleanup.
  - Gate: no server path receives VMK or S_user. No plaintext left after a failed Coder run.
- [ ] **V7, Connections** (#11238): Drive token as a vault object, `drive.read` inside the enclave.
  - Gate: Drive contents never reach openagents-web.

Owner steps (GCP project and org deny policy, Vertex abuse-monitoring exception) go to `NEEDS_OWNER.md` when their milestone starts.

queries.title: Private inference: attested Pylons and sealed jobs over Nostr (NIP-ATT)
queries.body:
Owner request, 2026-10-10: private inference over Nostr, our own version of the ideas in Darkbloom (d-inference; proprietary licence, ideas only) and Tinfoil.

**Spec:** `docs/security/private-inference.md`. **Wire format:** draft `nips/openagents/NIP-ATT.md`. Releases `3202`, release heads `30202`, attested endpoints `30203`, and the `openagents.attested.v1` sealed-job feature for CJ/DEC, with receipts that use ciphertext digests and name the measurement.

**Shape:**
- The client verifies the Pylon's TEE evidence and the release itself, then NIP-44 seals the job to the attested endpoint key (gift-wrap optional).
- Our gateway and relays carry ciphertext only.
- Trust levels are computed from evidence: `open`, `hardened` (Mac, not private), `tee`, and `tee-cloud`. Vault and financial data need `tee-cloud`.
- Vertex is never "private".

**Milestones:**
- [ ] **P0.** NIP-ATT types and validators in `crates/nostr`, plus a Confidential Space PKI token verifier (Rust + WASM).
  - Gate: fixtures for debug image, wrong digest, binding mismatch, expiry and rollback.
- [ ] **P1.** Reproducible Psionic inference image with a pinned open model or Clef, Rekor, and `3202`/`30202` publishing.
  - Gate: a second builder matches the digest.
- [ ] **P2.** One spot `a3-highgpu-1g` (TDX + H100) Confidential Space node publishing `30203` and serving `openagents.attested.v1` decisions and chat.
  - Gate: a canary prompt never appears in the gateway, relay or logs, and the client refuses a debug-image node.
- [ ] **P3.** Gateway pass-through and level routing (#11225 `/v1/systemone`), receipts, and web/app verification.
  - Gate: a vault Private turn end to end on production.
- [ ] **P4.** Third-party `tee` Pylons (raw TDX/SNP/NVIDIA evidence) and a `hardened` Mac level.

queries.title: Issue flow: --land queue hands green changes to the landing queue
queries.body:
The issue flow (`openagents chat work --issues N --land main|pr`, `coder::task::issue_run`) lands each green change itself (rebase + push per issue, `landing::land`). The landing queue from #11227 (`openagents land submit`, `oa-land-worker` on `oa-dev-env-1`, docs/cloud/land-queue.md) is meant to be the one serial integrator for every machine, but the issue flow cannot hand a change to it: `--land` accepts only `main` or `pr`.

Do:
- Add `Land::Queue` (`--land queue`; also accepted in `.openagents/coder-issues.json` policy). After the flow's checks pass it commits as it does today, pushes the commit to `land/<entry id>` on origin, and submits a `coder::task::land_queue::Entry` (issue set, `close: true`, machine, head, summary = issue title) to the default queue (`OPENAGENTS_LAND_QUEUE` honoured). It does not close the issue itself: the integrator closes it when the entry lands, and comments the reason if it bounces.
- The flow's ending and the issue comment say the change was queued, with the entry id and branch; the flow link's outcome is `queued` (new word) and `commits` holds the pushed head.
- `chat_gce.rs` and `chat_boat.rs` run scripts pass `--land queue` through.
- Tests: parse, policy round-trip, and a flow test with a `Dir` queue that asserts the entry is written with the issue and the pushed head, and the issue is not closed by the flow.

Found while running the V1 self-driving loop on `oa-dev-env-1` (S1 inventory, docs/product/s1/).

queries.title: Trace replay: capture changes the issue flow and landing queue landed
queries.body:
`scripts/bench/traces/traces.py capture` reads only `coder issue-run` folders and briefed A/B results (docs/coder/traces.md). Changes landed by the issue flow (`openagents chat work --issues N`) or by the landing queue (#11227) leave no folder it can read, so the S1 inventory (docs/product/self-improving-codebases.md: every label replay-verified) cannot replay them.

Do:
- Add `capture --landed COMMIT --issue N [--check CMD ...]` (repeatable; several commits allowed as `--landed A,B`). The trace's `base` is `COMMIT~1`, the diff is `git diff COMMIT~1 COMMIT` stored by digest, `files_changed` from the diff, `source` `landed:<commit>`, `id` `landed:<short>-issue-N`, `outcome` `landed`, `cost` all components `null` with reason `not recorded by the issue flow` (never 0). `check_spec` defaults to the issue flow's gate for the touched Rust packages (`cargo test -p PKG` per package whose files changed; none for docs-only diffs, which then replay the diff/tree/files fields and report checks `none`), or the given `--check` commands. Recorded check results are the ones the landing reported: pass, stated as `recorded_by: issue_flow_gate`.
- `replay --on mac` must work on a Linux cloud environment too (it is "this computer"); add `--on local` as the clearer alias.
- Unit tests in `scripts/bench/traces/test_traces.py` for the new source with a temporary git repo.
- docs/coder/traces.md: a short "Landed commits" section.

Found while running the V1 self-driving loop on `oa-dev-env-1` (S1 inventory, docs/product/s1/).

queries.title: Web chat: "Summarize this repo" in a project chat answered with the install-Coder text
queries.body:
In a project chat on openagents.com (project "finances", repo AtlantisPleb/finances, branch main), "Summarize this repo." was answered with the generic install Coder / `coder login` text instead of a summary.

**Cause**
- The web chat never sent the chat's project to the worker: `answer()` filled `context.project` only from the old public-repository selection, not the composer's project and branch.
- Without that, Jev read "this repo" as OpenAgents (`codebase.kb`, `meta`, or `product.kb`, all at about 0.2 confidence). On the website, work routes become `WEB_NOTE`, the "install Coder, run coder login" instructions.
- Nothing on the web read the person's repository.

**Fix** (cba18936e3, 66c7a821fe)
- `openagents-web/src/repo_snapshot.rs` reads the project's repository on the chosen branch using the person's GitHub connection: description, languages, recent commits, file tree, README, and root manifests, within a 12 KB bound. It is sent as `context.repository`.
- In the worker, the snapshot goes into the model's instructions. Jev is told the chat is in the user's own repository, and a typed side question `repository` (read / change / other) is asked. On the website a sure `read` is answered by the model from the repository (`policy::in_project`, `REPO_NOTE`). Work and codebase routes never get the install text.
- Golden `project.summarize_repo` in bench/web-chat runs in router mode and is a critical golden. Live Jev scored repository `read` at 0.92-0.94 and gave tier model with the repo note.

**Deployed**
- Chat worker: release cba18936e3 (rollback: f04d57a58a).
- Website: revision coder-web-c1c2584707-20261010171153 (rollback: coder-web-3805219f10-20261010170423).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

queries.title: Vault tiers B and C: sealed hardware with your share, and honest logged Tier C (V0, V2-V5, V7)
queries.body:
Follow-up to #11240, which shipped Tier A (only you). The spec is docs/security/sensitive-data-vault.md; wire formats in nips/openagents/NIP-VAULT.md (the `sealed` and `operator` wraps, sessions, leases) and NIP-ATT.

Milestones still open (each gate in the spec's table):
- V0 Honest Tier C: CMEK on the chat bucket, KMS envelope for new attachments, KMS Data Access logs, vault/finances excluded from training.
- V2 Sealed key release: the vault GCP project, HSM key ring, attested WIP (TDX + STABLE + digest), deny policies, public audit export, the vault workload on c3-standard TDX. Owner denial test.
- V3 Release log and client checks (NIP-ATT heads, Rekor, reproducible build, 7-day delay, opt-in approval).
- V4 Tier B in the product: finances project vault, leases, Active access, export, crypto-shredding with KMS key versions.
- V5 Private route: a model in TDX + H100 Confidential Space (#11241).
- V7 Connections into the vault (Drive token as a vault object, drive.read in the enclave; #11238).

Built already and reusable: `crates/oa-vault` (VMK, slots, objects, index; vectors), `crates/oa-vault-web`, the web vault page and API, `openagents vault`.

queries.title: Vault, only you: the phone and Mac apps, and changing keys when a device is removed
queries.body:
Follow-up to #11240 (Tier A live on the web and in `openagents vault`).

- Apps: a Vault screen in OpenAgents iOS/Android (crates/openagents-mobile, its own workspace) on `crates/oa-vault`: a device slot in the Keychain (this device only) / Android Keystore, add the phone from a pairing link or QR (`/settings/vault#pair=...`), list/open/add/delete, and answers On this device (a local model) or Fast.
- Removing a device you suspect: rotate the vault master key (new VMK, every remaining slot resealed, which needs each method's secret, so the flow asks for the recovery code and re-adds the other devices; `Index::rewrap` already rewraps every file key). Today removing a device deletes its slot only, and the page says so.
- `Index::insert(entry)` for retrying an index write after a conflict without re-uploading (the CLI rebuilds it by hand).
- Attach a vault file to an ordinary chat turn: only if the answer is then kept as a vault object, never in the plain chat record.

queries.title: Router: cut the router set's tokens so a Clef door answers in under 1 s (ask cli_group and answer only when needed, shorter option descriptions)
queries.body:
## Problem

Each chat turn sends the split router (#11193) 24.7k Clef tokens in three requests:

| Request | Tokens |
|---|---|
| main | 9,535 |
| `answer` | 3,289 |
| `cli_group` | 11,830 |

Within the main request, `route` takes 5.1k tokens for 22 options.

The option descriptions average about 230 tokens each.

On one RTX 4080 the three requests queue on the device. The best Psionic Clef build, `7af29040e6`, takes 4.2 s for the set. The matrix multiplies alone have a floor of about 1.8 s at the card's peak.

Prefix reuse cannot help, because the 30–50-token state comes before the 24k-token schema.

So the under-1 s target for a Clef door needs fewer tokens, not faster prefill.

Numbers: `docs/inference/clef-native.md` ("The router set on one 4080", "Router quality") and https://github.com/OpenAgentsInc/openagents/issues/11195#issuecomment-6101244728.

## Scope

- **Ask `cli_group` only when needed.** Ask it only when the main request's route needs a CLI proposal, and `answer` only when the route can serve a prepared answer. This costs a second round trip on those turns, so measure it against `first::LATE`.
- **Shorten the option descriptions** for `route`, `cli_group` and `answer`. Aim for about 40–60 tokens per option.
- **Re-measure** the routes-v5 held-out eval and the web chat goldens (router mode) against Jev and the Clef door, with each model's calibration map (`calibration-v2`, `calibration-clef-flash-v1`, refit after the change).

## Done when

- A typical turn sends no more than about 6k Clef tokens.
- The set takes no more than 1 s on the CoderOS-4080 Pylon.
- Jev's router goldens score does not regress.

queries.title: Landing livelocks on a busy main: re-checks take longer than main's commit interval
queries.body:
Found by the S1 cloud run on `oa-dev-env-1` (docs/product/s1/). The issue flow's `--land main` (and the queue integrator, which uses the same `landing::land`) rebases onto `main` and re-runs the gate whenever the newer commits can affect the change. On the current `main` that loop does not converge:

- `main` took 38 commits in the last 3 hours (one every ~4.7 min), from agents pushing directly, mostly in the hot crates the issue flow touches (`openagents-web` 41 file-touches, `coder` 16, `openagents-cli` 15).
- One gate run for a change touching `coder`, `microcoder`, `openagents-chat`, `openagents-cli` (`cargo test -q -p … --all-features` each, plus a base re-run of any failing test) takes 25-35 min on a 22-vCPU environment.
- #11242: checks passed 17:48 UTC → `main` +11 → re-check passed 18:17 → `main` +5 → re-check passed ~19:05 → `main` +5 → re-check again (still landing at 19:30, 2.5 h after its turn ended). #11228: same pattern, and a change that touches `Cargo.lock` always re-checks.
- Two flows on one environment each build and test at `-j22`; load average reached 183 on 22 vCPUs, which roughly doubles every check.

The checks must keep passing on the exact change that lands (no weakening). Proposals, in order:
1. **One way onto `main`.** Agents on every machine land through the #11227 queue (`--land queue`, #11242) instead of pushing directly, so `main` moves only through the integrator and re-checks race nothing. A pre-receive-style rule (or the agent contract) makes direct pushes the exception.
2. **Merge train in the integrator.** Rebase the next K queued entries in order, run the union of their gates once on the stacked result, land all on green, bisect on red.
3. **Per-flow CPU share.** `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` / `RUST_TEST_THREADS` scaled to the slots in use, so two flows don't thrash one box.
4. **Cheaper re-check where sound.** After a rebase whose new commits touch only a dependency of the change, the re-check can reuse the previous run's test binaries for packages whose inputs did not change (fingerprint, not heuristics).

Acceptance: with the current commit rate, a change touching `coder` + `openagents-cli` lands within one gate run of its checks passing, with the checks passing on the exact landed tree.

queries.title: File finder: precompute file cards and tags offline; runtime is one embedding plus one tag decision (~1 s), no per-file model calls
Fleet rows for cloud runs: stage, cost so far, landing queue state and links
queries.body:
Follow-up to #11228 (owner priority, 2026-10-10): the owner watches the self-driving runs on the phone and the web and runs no commands. #11228 reports each `chat work` issue flow as an agent item (`crates/openagents-cli/src/chat_fleet.rs` → `coder_sync::activity`), shown on the phone's Agents screen (`GET /v1/agents`) and `/settings/agents`. Make each row say what the owner needs, using only fields the server already sends so the phone needs no new build:

- **Stage** in the item's `line`, from the flow's events: `finding files`, `coding`, `checks`, `fix turn N`, `landing` (rebase / re-check / push), `queued` (with the land-queue entry), `landed <commit10>`, `failed: <one-line reason>`.
- **Time**: `started_unix` / `finished_unix` kept right across fix turns.
- **Cost so far**: `cost_usd` and `tokens` updated after every turn from the task's ATIF traces (Claude Code's reported `cost_usd`; `None` when unknown, never 0), plus the decision call's cost.
- **Landing queue state**: one item per open land-queue entry (`gs://openagentsgemini-coder-artifacts/land-queue/openagents`, `coder::task::land_queue`), kind `landing`, title the entry summary, `line` its state (`queued`, `landing: checks`, `landed <commit>`, `bounced: <reason>`), reported by the integrator (`openagents land work` on `oa-dev-env-1`).
- **Links**: the item title starts `#N` and the web agents panel (#11164, and `/settings/agents`) renders the issue and commit as links to GitHub. Check whether the phone already links `#N`; if it needs a new build for links, say so and leave links web-only.

Acceptance: with a run on `oa-dev-env-1`, the owner signed in on openagents.com sees the row move through the stages with time and cost, sees the queue entry, and can click the issue and the commit; the phone shows the same rows without a new build (verified against the phone's renderer in `crates/openagents-mobile`). Tests from fixture event streams for each stage; deployed to staging and checked signed in.

queries.title: Hardened Mac Pylons: Psionic runs inside a locked-down process with a Secure Enclave–bound key (NIP-ATT trust level `hardened`)
queries.body:
Owner, 2026-10-10: build our own version of the Darkbloom (Layr-Labs/d-inference) hardened provider, for Mac Pylons. Ideas only, no code: their licence is proprietary. Design: docs/security/private-inference.md (trust levels `open` / `hardened` / `tee` / `tee-cloud`) and nips/openagents/NIP-ATT.md.

**Build:**
- **In-process inference.** The Pylon decrypts and runs Psionic (Clef and language models, Metal) inside one process, with no local server, subprocess or IPC carrying plaintext.
- **Runtime hardening.** Hardened Runtime and a notarized, signed binary; `PT_DENY_ATTACH`; library validation; no `get-task-allow`. Refuse to serve unless SIP and Secure Boot are on, with the checks repeated periodically.
- **Key.** A P-256 key generated in and bound to the Secure Enclave, non-exportable, used for the job-sealing key agreement (or to sign an ephemeral X25519 key). The private key never exists in memory.
- **Evidence.** App Attest (or Apple Managed Device Attestation where enrolled) proving a genuine, untampered build of our binary. Publish it as NIP-ATT evidence plus the binary's code-signing identity and hash, matched against our release log.
- **Re-check.** Challenge-response every few minutes (fresh Secure Enclave signature, SIP still on). A Pylon that fails drops back to `open`.
- **Data hygiene.** Plaintext never touches disk, swap is locked where possible, logs are content-free, and memory is zeroed after each job.

**Honest label.** `hardened` raises the bar against a casual operator. It does not stop someone who controls the hardware and the OS. The page and API must never call it private or sealed.

**Done when:** a Mac Pylon advertises `hardened` with verifiable evidence, a client checks it and seals a job to it, and a tamper test (unsigned binary, SIP off, debugger attach) drops it to `open` or refuses the job.

queries.title: Route jobs by trust level: private data only to tee/tee-cloud; hardened and open labelled; the client verifies before sealing
queries.body:
Follow-up to NIP-ATT (#11241) and the hardened Mac Pylons issue (https://github.com/OpenAgentsInc/openagents/issues/11251).

- **Requirements on jobs.** Every NIP-DEC or inference job carries a minimum trust level. Vault data, Drive and financial sources, and anything the user marks private require `tee` or `tee-cloud`. Ordinary work may use `hardened` or `open`.
- **Client checks.** The client (web, apps, CLI, gateway) checks the provider's evidence for that level before sealing, and refuses providers below the requirement.
- **Labels in the UI.** Every answer says which trust level and provider ran it ("sealed hardware", "hardened Mac, its owner could still read it", "open").
- **Beacons and dispatch.** NIP-PYLON beacons advertise the level with evidence references, and the gateway dispatch (#11225 path) filters by it.

**Done when:** a vault-file question can never be served by an `open` or `hardened` Pylon, which a test proves, and the /att page lets a visitor pick a level and see the refusal when the requirement isn't met.

queries.title: Actor primitive
queries.body:
Build our own actor primitive, taking ideas from Rivet Actors without depending on Rivet. The owner approved this on 2026-10-10. This issue is infrastructure and is not on the V1 launch board.

**Spec:** [docs/architecture/actors.md](https://github.com/OpenAgentsInc/openagents/blob/main/docs/architecture/actors.md)

## Summary

An actor is keyed by `(type, workspace_id, key)` and has:
- typed state, stored as one `jsonb` row in a new `actor` schema in the `openagents` Cloud SQL database;
- typed actions, a durable ordered inbox, at-least-once alarms (one-shot and cron), and effects run after commit;
- work items that remote executors claim, heartbeat and finish, fenced by an epoch;
- durable, sequenced events that web and phone receive over SSE.

How it runs:
- **Single writer:** each transition is one transaction under `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the actor's row. The row's `version` is the fencing token, so there is no long-held lease and placement does not matter for correctness.
- **Outbox:** state, events, sends, alarms and effects commit together.
- **Cross-process wake-up:** `pg_notify`, as the relay already does.
- **Deployment:** no new service, broker or cache. The runtime is linked into `openagents-web`.

## Migration order (each step gets its own issue)

0. Runtime crate `crates/actors`, with tests, a load tool and an admin `openagents actor` command.
1. Landing queue. It goes first because it is internal and has the most correctness gaps: unfenced takes, a stale heartbeat during checks, a crash after push that bounces a landed change, and double submits.
2. Fleet rows and web fleet runs (#11228, #11164). These prove fan-out to web and phone. `GET /v1/agents` keeps its shape.
3. Mac jobs (#11223).
4. Own-runs.
5. Scheduled prompts (#11177).
6. Dev-environment idle stop.

Decision dispatch's beacon book, the chat worker's NIP-CJ admission and the local background runner stay as they are; the spec gives the reasons.

## Open questions for the owner

Section 14 of the spec lists them:
- Postgres directly in the web binary
- lifting the one-replica pin
- Cloud SQL high availability
- the migration order
- history retention
- whether actors ever run on user machines
- the Effect Native contract path
- a durable chat-worker queue

queries.title: Coder: no vendor names by default (composer says auto, auto runs on OpenAgents), Claude Code-style transcript, Cmd+A selects the input
queries.body:
Owner, 2026-10-10: the coder-new composer rail showed `openai/gpt-6-luna:none` ("I don't want to advertise other people's products").

- The rail shows `auto` unless the person picked a model in /models; then only the model's name, without vendor prefix or settings like `:none`. Same for the /models default row, OpenRouter settings page, and `coder status`.
- The per-reply `model · time` footer is removed.
- `auto` runs first on the OpenAgents inference gateway (`openagents/auto`, Vertex first) with the signed-in session; it falls back to the OpenRouter free router or the local loop before any words, without naming OpenRouter. Pinned models keep #11132 (no failover).
- Transcript matches Claude Code: user row in column 0 on a highlight band, `●` bullets with hanging indents, `⎿` results, one blank line between items.
- Cmd+A selects only the composer text (kitty keyboard protocol), with Cmd+C/Cmd+X, Ctrl+Shift+A fallback.
- Tests that save settings refuse the real ~/.openagents.

queries.title: Settings → Claude: Connect your Claude subscription in three steps (dialog, page fallback, composer card)
queries.body:
Settings → Claude: lead with a "Connect your Claude subscription" flow for the subscription-token allowlist.

- A dialog (openagents-ui `Dialog`) with three steps: run `claude setup-token` on your own computer (code block with a copy button, link to Anthropic's install page); sign in with your Claude Pro or Max account and approve; paste the `sk-ant-oat…` token (about-this-token link). Cancel, and Connect subscription, disabled until the field matches the token's shape.
- Without script, the same steps are a plain page at `/settings/claude/subscription`.
- Submit: malformed tokens are refused before Anthropic is asked; then the existing check with Anthropic (#11204); then kept sealed. Plain errors for refused or malformed tokens.
- Afterwards Settings shows "Claude subscription connected" with the fingerprint and Remove.
- Signing in inside the environment and the key form (#11235) stay below as alternatives.
- The composer's Connect Claude card (#11234) opens the same dialog over the page and returns to the chat.
- Allowlist unchanged (`OPENAGENTS_WEB_CLAUDE_TOKEN_ACCOUNTS`, default owner only): accounts off the list see none of it.

queries.title: Own Boat backend on GCE: Boat SDK against our Google Cloud, hosted Boat off by default
queries.body:
Hosted Boat's API returned 502 from about 23:05 UTC on 2026-10-10, and openagents.com Environments were switched off at revision start because the studio could not open.

Owner directive: stop using hosted Boat; run the Boat SDK against our own backend on Google Cloud.

Scope:
1. `crates/oa-boat`: a Rust service that answers the subset of Boat's v1 API we call (sandboxes create/get/list/delete with size classes, stop/resume/fork, commands sync/detached/NDJSON stream, files, usage, limits, named snapshots as GCE images, latest snapshot), backed by GCE VMs from `oa-coder-host` (spot for batch, on-demand for interactive), TTL and idle stop. Deployed on Cloud Run (`oa-boat`), auth by our own token in Secret Manager.
2. `crates/boat` defaults to our service; boat.dev only with an explicit `BOAT_HOSTED=1`.
3. Environments never decided once at startup: the studio is retried in the background and a backend outage shows "Environments are temporarily unavailable".
4. The daily `oa-coder-main-<date>` template builds on our backend as a GCE image.

Verify on staging, then production: create an environment, run a Claude Code task, files back, stop; daily template; idle stop; cost per hour; `--on boat` users.

queries.title: briefed-agent: the run summary says how verify went (calls, failures, passed, last status)
queries.body:
The briefed agent (`crates/briefed-agent`) writes `summary.json` at the end of a run, but it does not say how its `verify` tool went. A caller that has to decide whether to fall back to bare Claude Code (the `openagents work` engine, `scripts/work/work_issue.py`) has to re-read and parse the `verify.jsonl` log itself, and a config without a `verify.log` path leaves no record at all.

Change: count `verify` calls in the run and add a `verify` object to `summary.json`:

- `calls`: verify calls that ran (cached answers included),
- `failures`: calls whose status was not `pass` or `compiles`,
- `passed`: whether any call returned `pass`,
- `last`: the status of the last call, or `null` when verify never ran.

Keep `check_runs` as it is. Add a unit test for the counting.

queries.title: Work on an issue: the briefed agent is the default engine on web, API and CLI
queries.body:
Make the briefed agent (#11211: -53.9% cost per accepted change, 2.3x faster, same success rate; docs/inference/briefed-agent-ab.md) the default engine whenever someone asks for an issue to be worked: openagents.com (chat, project chat, GitHub tools, agent fleet runs, Claude Code runs), the API, and the CLI.

1. **One engine entry point.** "Work on issue N in repo R": build the briefing (filefind + brief generator), run the briefed agent with `verify` (#11229) in a cloud environment from the `oa-coder-host` image, signed in with the requesting person's own Claude credential. Judge by the actual diff and replayed checks. On success land through the landing queue or open a PR, as asked. On escalation (low briefing confidence, repeated verify failures, a missing capability) fall back to bare Claude Code and record why.
2. **Every entry point uses it.** Web "Work on this issue" (project chat, GitHub tools, a pasted issue link through the typed router, agent fleet runs); `POST /v1/work {repo, issue, land: queue|pr}` with status and SSE progress; `openagents chat work` defaults to it, `--engine bare` opts out.
3. **Visible results.** Engine, time, cost (unknown stays unknown), checks, PR or commit; live progress where #11228's run rows appear.
4. **Proof.** 3 real open issues through production, each next to a bare Claude Code run on the same issue.

queries.title: Web: the /att page's error text has machine talk ("lane", "attested"), so copy_guard fails
queries.body:
`cargo test -p openagents-web --lib copy_guard` fails on main:

```
machine talk in the site's copy (rewrite it in plain words, see AGENTS.md):
crates/openagents-web/src/pages/att.rs:444: "attested" in "this lane has no attested records"
crates/openagents-web/src/pages/att.rs:444: "lane" in "this lane has no attested records"
crates/openagents-web/src/pages/att.rs:908: "lane" in "The request is not addressed to the lane's machine."
```

Both strings can reach a person on /att. Rewrite them in plain words (say what happened: no checked records for this machine yet; the request was sent to a different machine), keeping their meaning, so the copy guard passes.

queries.title: briefed-agent: verify.jsonl skips answers from the cache, so callers undercount verify calls
queries.body:
`crates/briefed-agent/src/verify.rs` appends one line to the `verify` log (`verify.log`) per call in `run_uncached`, but a call answered from the cache (an unchanged candidate) returns before that and writes nothing. The run's log then says fewer calls than the agent made, and a caller reading it (the `openagents work` engine counts failing calls to decide when to hand over to Claude Code) undercounts repeated failures.

Change: log every call, the cached ones too, with `"cached": true` on those, and keep the same fields (`filter`, `fast`, `final`, `status`, `secs`). Add a unit test that a repeated call on an unchanged worktree writes two lines, the second cached.

queries.title: briefed-agent: a symlink inside the worktree lets a file tool reach outside it
queries.body:
`crates/briefed-agent/src/main.rs` keeps the file tools (Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep) inside the task's worktree with `inside()`, which resolves the tool's path **lexically** (`resolve()` drops `.` and `..`) and checks the prefix. A symlink in the worktree that points outside it (a checked-in link, or one the agent's own Write can't make but the repo already has) passes that check: `Read worktree/link/secret` is allowed although the file is outside the worktree.

Change: after the lexical check, resolve the longest existing ancestor of the path with `canonicalize` and require it to be inside the canonical worktree too; deny (and record in `denied`) otherwise. A path whose parents don't exist yet (a new file) is judged by its existing ancestor. Add unit tests: a symlinked directory pointing outside is denied; a normal new file inside is allowed.

queries.title: briefed-agent: writing a brand-new file counts as a briefing miss
queries.body:
`crates/briefed-agent/src/main.rs` `observe()` records a **miss** (a file the briefing should have listed) for an `Edit`/`MultiEdit`/`Write` of a file the briefing did not list and the agent had not read. A `Write` that creates a file that did not exist at the base commit (a new test file, a new module) is counted too, although no finder could have listed it. These misses feed the context finder's feedback (#11210, `filefind feedback --ab`), so new files show up as false finder failures.

Change: when observing a `Write`, a path that does not exist in the worktree at that moment (the file is being created) is recorded in `files_written` but is not a miss. Edits of existing unlisted files stay misses. Add unit tests for both.
